sections.h2: Where is Norfolk, Virginia, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Norfolk is an independent city in the southeastern corner of Virginia, where the Elizabeth River meets the Chesapeake Bay. It is not part of any county, so the city handles its own assessments, tax billing and zoning.

The city covers 96.41 square miles, but only 53.28 of those are land. The other 43.13 square miles are water, and the average elevation is about 6.9 feet. The 2020 census counted 238,005 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 231,013.

Norfolk sits at the center of Hampton Roads, a metro area of more than 1.8 million people. Virginia Beach and Chesapeake are larger by population, which makes Norfolk the third-largest city in the region and fourth in the state.

sections.h2: How did Norfolk grow into the city it is today?
sections.html:
Norfolk began as a colonial seaport in the late 1600s and received a royal borough charter in 1736. It was incorporated as a city in 1845.

The Navy shaped the modern city. The 1907 Jamestown Exposition at Sewell's Point led to a naval air station in 1917, which became Naval Station Norfolk, the largest naval base in the world.

The city also grew by annexation. It took in Berkley in 1906, then Sewell's Point, Willoughby Spit, Campostella and Ocean View in 1923. Later annexations in 1955 and 1959, plus a 1988 land swap with Virginia Beach, set today's borders.

Highway building changed where people lived. The Downtown Tunnel opened in 1952, the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel in 1957, the Midtown Tunnel in 1962 and the Virginia Beach-Norfolk Expressway in 1967. Those links helped suburbs form and pulled residents out of older neighborhoods.

sections.h2: Which Norfolk neighborhoods do sellers hear about most?
sections.html:
Norfolk has dozens of named neighborhoods, and the age and style of the houses change from one to the next. These are the ones that Wikipedia singles out.

  • Freemason and West Freemason: historic downtown neighborhoods with some of the oldest buildings in the city.
  • Berkley: a former separate city, annexed in 1906 and located across the Elizabeth River.
  • Willoughby Spit and Ocean View: bay-front areas with a long link to the Chesapeake Bay.
  • Ghent, Colonial Place, Larchmont, North Shore, Edgewater and Lafayette Shores: popular residential areas.
  • Downtown, Ghent and Fairmount Park: areas changed by revitalization over recent decades.

A pre-war rowhouse in Ghent, a bayside house in Ocean View and a mid-century home in Larchmont each bring different repair and flood questions. That is why a fast sale often starts with a walk-through, not a formula.

sections.h2: What does Norfolk's climate and flooding mean for a house?
sections.html:
Norfolk has a humid subtropical climate, and flooding is the main building concern. The city is low, mostly surrounded by water and slowly subsiding, and some areas already flood at high tide.

Summers are warm and humid, with 90 degree days on average 35 times a year. Winters are mild, with about 6.2 inches of snow in a typical season. The highest tropical storm risk runs from mid-August through September, when heavy rain and wind can reach the city.

The City of Norfolk publishes flood zone rules on its Flood Zones page. The Flood Insurance Rate Map from FEMA sets the zones, and the city enforces them through Article 3.9.7 of its zoning ordinance and the Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code. The city lists these zones:

  • X: outside the 0.2% annual chance flood area, the least likely to flood.
  • X shaded: 0.2% annual chance, with depths under 1 foot in a 1% flood.
  • AE, AH and AO: 1% annual chance zones, with base flood elevations in AE.
  • VE: velocity zone with waves of 3 feet or more.

Norfolk runs a public tool called Forerunner where anyone can look up a property's zone and find elevation certificates. A buyer will probably check the same data, so a seller who has looked first avoids surprises.

sections.h2: How does the Navy and port economy affect Norfolk sellers?
sections.html:
Government spending, mostly military, is the largest part of Norfolk's economy. Naval Station Norfolk is the headquarters of U.S. Fleet Forces Command, which Wikipedia describes as covering more than 62,000 active-duty personnel, 75 ships and 132 aircraft. The base also hosts a NATO command.

The Virginia Port Authority is headquartered in the city and operates Norfolk International Terminals. Maersk Line, Limited and several other shipping firms have North American offices here. Sentara Health is also headquartered in Norfolk.

For sellers, this can mean timing set by orders. A military household that gets new orders may need to close in a few weeks, and a landlord with a tenant on a short lease may want out before the next rotation. Cash sales fit those schedules because there is no loan approval to wait on.

sections.h2: How are real estate taxes billed in Norfolk?
sections.html:
The City Assessor sets the value, the City Council sets the rate, and the Treasurer collects the bill. Taxes follow a July 1 to June 30 fiscal year and are paid quarterly.

  • First quarter: due September 30.
  • Second quarter: due December 5.
  • Third quarter: due March 31.
  • Fourth quarter: due June 5.

The Treasurer bills more than 68,000 taxable parcels and mails bills at least 30 days ahead. For assessment questions, call the City Assessor's Office at 757-664-4732. The Treasurer's Real Estate Tax page also lists tax relief contacts at the Department of Human Services.

The same page notes that the Treasurer collects nuisance abatement liens sent over by Neighborhood Quality, with 30 days to pay. If a Norfolk house has had weeds, trash or structure problems cleaned up by the city, ask the Treasurer for a payoff before you list or sign a contract.

Unpaid real estate tax can end in a public sale. The Treasurer's page shows an online auction held under Virginia Code 58.1-3975 in June 2026 for delinquent parcels.

sections.h2: What does it take to sell a Norfolk house for cash?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Norfolk follows the same Virginia deed rules as any other sale, but it skips the loan and the repair list. The steps are short.

  • Gather the deed, the latest tax bill and any payoff letters.
  • Check for city liens, including nuisance abatement charges.
  • Look up the flood zone on Forerunner.
  • Choose a settlement company and sign the contract.

On the deed, Virginia charges a grantor tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value, which the seller normally pays unless the contract says otherwise. The deed must show the price on its first page before the clerk will record it. Ask your settlement agent for the exact figures on your sale.

sections.h2: What do Norfolk sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Most Norfolk sellers deal with a handful of repeat problems, and the location explains many of them.

  • Water damage in crawl spaces, basements and first floors on low lots.
  • Older houses with outdated wiring, plumbing or roofs.
  • Inherited houses with several heirs and no clear next step.
  • Rental properties with tenants, deferred repairs or city notices.
  • Back taxes or city liens that need to be paid at closing.

Any of these can slow a listing, since buyers who need a loan often ask for repairs. A direct sale lets the seller pick a closing date and hand over the house as it stands.

faqs.q: Is Norfolk a city or a county?
faqs.a: Norfolk is an independent city. It is not inside a county, so the city handles assessments, tax bills and zoning itself.

faqs.q: When are Norfolk real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Norfolk bills quarterly, with due dates of September 30, December 5, March 31 and June 5. The fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30, according to the City Treasurer.

faqs.q: How do I check whether my Norfolk house is in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Use the city's Forerunner site, linked from the Flood Zones page. It shows the zone, flood data and any elevation certificates on file for a property.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Norfolk house with unpaid city liens?
faqs.a: Yes, but the liens are normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff on any nuisance abatement charge and the settlement agent for the rest.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia grantor tax on a Norfolk sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays unless the contract says the buyer will cover some or all of it. The rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value under Virginia Code 58.1-802.

faqs.q: Where can I ask about my Norfolk assessment?
faqs.a: Call the City Assessor's Office at 757-664-4732. For local permit or zoning rules that this page does not cover, ask the city office directly.
